name: io.megido/observed-revenue-market-research
title: Megido: niche, competitor and traffic research on sites with observed revenue
description: Niche, competitor and traffic research on 400K+ websites with observed revenue, as MCP tools.

tools.name: capabilities
tools.description: List the tools this server exposes and what each one charges for, what the corpus is, the closed vocabularies their filters accept — countries, site types, niche levels (cohort_levels; level 1 holds the narrowest niches and each higher level groups the niches of the level below), index axes, banding schemes with their numeric boundaries — the per-call limits in force for your organization, its plan and the free quota the plan includes, and the disclosure rules that govern what is returned before and after a project is revealed. Free. Call it once at the start of a session instead of guessing filter values: unknown values are rejected, not ignored. Its vocabularies and prices are the same from call to call; the plan, quota and limits it reports follow your organization, so read it again after your user registers; what your organization has left to spend is in usage.

tools.name: usage
tools.description: Report the calling organization's plan, the free quota it has left this period and the day the quota renews, its balance, the credits its agents' tasks hold and what is left available to spend, the coverage it has left for the current period, the per-call limits in force, how many projects it holds revealed and how many profile parts it currently holds. Free. Consult it before planning a wide search: coverage limits how many new entities you can see in a period; the free quota and the available credits (the balance less what agents' tasks hold) limit what you can pay for. What the tools accept and charge for is in capabilities.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: Return the client guide in full, as Markdown: what the corpus is and what it cannot tell, how to read every field and band, what each call costs and spends, the recommended order of work, recipes for common questions and how to report results to your user. Free. Read it at the start of a session when the server instructions are not in your context, and whenever you are unsure how to read a field or what a call will cost.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Send feedback to the Megido team: a bug, wrong or missing data, a feature request or anything else, with the ids of the projects or niches it is about. Send it when your user asks, and on your own when a call fails unexpectedly, the data contradicts itself or the corpus lacks something your user needs; then tell your user what you sent. Write what happened and what you expected, and leave out personal details the message does not need. Free, within a daily limit per organization: past it the call is refused with limit_exceeded. The organization sees its feedback and the team's progress on it in the portal.

tools.name: search_cohorts
tools.description: Find market niches either by describing them in words or by conditions on the niche itself: size, level in the hierarchy, median quality index, share of growing members (members whose visits grew by more than 10% over the last month), leading country. Every project underneath these niches is a site where revenue has been observed, so a niche here is a market rather than a topic. Returns niche ids with a gloss, the number of member projects and a quality summary — never their member sites. With text, the results are the niches closest in meaning; sorting by size, index or growth then orders the closest ones only, as many as relevance_pool_cohorts in capabilities. Costs the base price plus the first-seen price for every niche shown to your organization for the first time this period, and each such niche spends one unit of coverage; call with estimate: true to see the price and get a quote_token first. This is the cheapest way into a market: use it before searching for projects when the user cannot yet name a single site in the space.

Index and growth are shares of members, so without filters.min_size niches of a few members come first

tools.name: get_cohort
tools.description: Open one niche: its gloss with labeling confidence, size, the distribution of its members over quality index bands, scale bands, growth bands, countries and site types in whole percents, its position in the hierarchy — parent, children, neighboring niches — and a stable sample of member projects as cards. Opening the niche itself spends no coverage; every parent, child, neighbor and sample member shown to your organization for the first time this period costs the first-seen price on top of the base price and spends one unit of coverage, so ask only for the parts you need. Use the hierarchy to widen or narrow the market definition instead of searching again. It takes a niche id: to find a niche by words or by conditions use search_cohorts.

tools.name: search_projects
tools.description: Find projects by a description of the idea, by similarity to one or more projects already on hand, or by conditions on their measured profile — quality axes, scale band, growth direction, country, site type — in any combination. Every project in the corpus is a site where revenue has been observed; how much a site earns and what it charges is not part of this corpus. Returns cards: id, short description, site type, quality index, scale band, growth, main country and niche. The domain appears only on projects your organization has revealed; reveal_project turns a card into a domain. With text or seed projects, the results are the projects closest in meaning, the seeds themselves left out; sorting by index, scale or growth then orders the closest ones only, as many as relevance_pool in capabilities. Costs the base price plus the first-seen price for every project shown to your organization for the first time this period, and each such project spends one unit of coverage; without limit a call returns as many rows as list_max in capabilities allows. Call with estimate: true to see the price and get a quote_token first. Use it when your user describes a kind of site or the niche is already known; for a market question start with search_cohorts, and for a domain your user already has use lookup_domain.

tools.name: get_project_card
tools.description: Open one or more projects: the short description, the quality index broken down by axis with an explanation of what each axis measures, the site type, the niches the project belongs to and its nearest neighbors by meaning. Use it to decide whether a project is worth revealing. A revealed project also lists its other domains (regional versions, mirrors). It returns no domain for projects your organization has not revealed and no traffic figures beyond the scale and growth bands of the card. The projects you open spend no coverage; every neighbor and niche shown to your organization for the first time this period costs the first-seen price on top of the base price and spends one unit of coverage, so leave out the parts you do not need. For its traffic use get_audience, get_channels and get_keywords.

tools.name: lookup_domain
tools.description: Check whether given domains are in the corpus. A hit returns a revealed card (project id, domain, short description, site type, quality index, scale and growth bands, main country, niche and, when known, the payment service), the project's other domains (regional versions, mirrors) and the profile parts available for the project. This is the only tool that accepts a raw domain; a scheme, a path, a leading www and a trailing dot are stripped, other subdomains are kept and usually miss. A domain known as another address of a project in the corpus (a regional version, a mirror or a redirect) returns that project, with mirror_of naming its domain. Every distinct submitted domain is charged the base price, including those not found unless charges_empty of lookup_domain in capabilities is false; a miss returns found: false and nothing else. A hit reveals the project to your organization for as many days as reveal_ttl_days in capabilities at no reveal price, exactly as reveal_project would, and spends one unit of coverage if your organization has not seen the project this period; reveal_project adds nothing for a project found here.

tools.name: reveal_project
tools.description: Turn project ids into domains, along with the project's other domains (regional versions, mirrors) and, when known, the service through which the project entered the corpus: a payment service or platform on whose page its visitors complete payment. Costs the base price plus the reveal price for every project your organization has not already revealed, by this tool or by a lookup_domain hit; a newly revealed project also spends one unit of coverage if it was not seen this period. A reveal lasts for the whole organization as many days as capabilities reports in reveal_ttl_days: while it holds, every later response shows the domain automatically at no further charge, revealing the project again neither charges nor extends it, and after it lapses the project is anonymous again until revealed anew. Reveal only the projects your user needs named: descriptions, bands and niches are readable without it. For a domain your user already has, lookup_domain finds and reveals its project without the reveal price.

tools.name: get_audience
tools.description: Return the audience profile of a project: monthly visits averaged over the last twelve months, unique visitors, deduplicated audience, annual visits, month-over-month change, visit duration, pages per visit, bounce rate, device split and the top countries with their shares and changes. Before a project is revealed the figures come as bands and the global, country and industry ranks are withheld, because a rank identifies the site outright; after a reveal the ranks are included, and precision: exact returns exact values instead of bands. Costs the base price plus the audience price for every project whose audience your organization does not already hold, and with precision: exact a surcharge for every revealed project on every call; a project without an audience layer comes back with profile null and is charged neither the part nor the exact surcharge. Ask in bands first, and for exact values only when your user needs exact numbers.

tools.name: get_channels
tools.description: Return where a project's traffic comes from: the marketing channels with their shares and the leading social platforms with their shares of the social traffic. Before a reveal only the three leading channels and the three leading social platforms are returned, as bands: a full channel mix is close to a fingerprint and would identify the site without paying for it; after a reveal every channel and platform in the data is returned, and precision: exact returns exact shares instead of bands. Costs the base price plus the channels price for every project whose channels your organization does not already hold, and with precision: exact a surcharge for every revealed project on every call; a project without a channels layer comes back with profile null and is charged neither the part nor the exact surcharge. Ask in bands first, and for exact values only when your user needs exact numbers.

tools.name: get_keywords
tools.description: Return the search demand behind a project: the branded and non-branded split of its organic search traffic, the top organic queries with their shares and month-over-month change, and, with include_paid, the top paid queries. Individual queries identify a site in any search tool, so before a reveal only the split is returned. After a reveal, each query's month-over-month change is an exact number even with precision: band. Costs the base price plus the keywords price for every project whose keywords your organization does not already hold, and with precision: exact a surcharge for every revealed project on every call; a project without search data comes back with profile null and is charged neither the part nor the exact surcharge. Ask in bands first, and for exact values only when your user needs exact numbers.
